messages:
simon: Ran a quick nsys on the prod-replay (stable-v3) to look at the KV cache behavior under mixed batch sizes. timeline shows a repeating pattern where one of the kernels spikes and we get a follow-up burst of `kv_evict_async` a few ms later. attaching perf link: https://perfetto.example/trace/2112233445 :eyes:

tara: Can you paste the top kernel table? is it a single kernel or a set that alternates?

simon: Top kernels by total time (from nsys summary):
```
1) attn_kv_load                    42.3%  (hot path)
2) matmul_small                    18.1%
3) kv_evict_async                  15.7%  (clustered after attn_kv_load)
4) softmax_reduce                  8.9%
5) memcpy_h2d                      3.2%
```
Looks like attn_kv_load triggers cache pressure, then eviction happens.

ben: That pattern smells like an eviction hysteresis bug — if we evict eagerly when occupancy crosses X, then a slightly bigger batch will miss and cause another eviction, oscillation. Were you profiling with prefix caching enabled?

simon: prefix cache ON. I also saw SM util drop to ~22% during the eviction bursts, then recover to ~78%. occupancy plots attached in the trace.

devon: Two quick checks: 1) are we demoting entries synchronously or enqueuing async evict work? 2) what's the batch size distribution in the replay? small tail could trigger repeated evicts.

perf-bot: nsys summary (abridged): total GPU time 1m12s; top 3 kernels: attn_kv_load (31s), matmul_small (13s), kv_evict_async (11s). Avg SM Util: 61% but per-window variance high (min 18%, max 92%).

tara: If kv_evict_async is 15% of time that's pretty expensive. Could we throttle eviction to off-peak (e.g., only once per X requests or when free slots < threshold)?

ben: We tried a time-gated eviction before but saw memory creep. Idea: change heuristic to prefer LRU with soft-threshold + background GC worker that only runs if GPU idle for >Y ms. That avoids mid-window GC.

simon: Repro steps I used:
```
# run trace
nsys profile --output trace.nsys --trace=cuda,cudnn --force-overwrite \ 
  --sample=none --stop-on-exit --target-processes all --cuda-memory-usage \ 
  ./replay --profile-mode --seed=7832 --batch-dist="[1,2,3,8,16]"
```
Attached `trace.nsys` and perfetto link. Also capture of kernel timeline shows eviction always within 2-8ms after attn_kv_load peak.

devon: Could be our eviction policy uses a reactive metric (recent load) instead of running-average; that would explain short-term oscillation. I'll instrument the eviction decision to log recent occupancy windows (10ms bins).

tara: Also check if `attn_kv_load` has a persistent long tail (slow warps) when batch mixes small+large. If it's warp-serialized it will inflate perceived trigger rate.

ben: Quick mitigation we can deploy to dedicated for next canary: increase eviction_threshold by 12% and enable background_gc=1. Low risk and reversible. Thoughts?

simon: SGTM. I'll produce a short patch + rollout plan and include a perf regression guard (compare nvprof top-k before/after).

perf-bot: perf regression guard created: job/evict-threshold-canary-211223 — will run 1k replay requests and post summary.

simon: Next actions:
- devon: add occupancy window logs and push to sim infra (ETA today)
- ben: PR for threshold bump + background GC toggle (ETA tomorrow morning)
- tara: run additional nsys with seeded batch tails to validate
- simon: coordinate canary and watch SM util / kv_evict_async pct

ben: I'll also add a small micro-benchmark that reproduces the oscillation pattern so we can run quick CI checks.

simon: thanks, folks. if we get the canary results we can decide whether to keep heuristic or move to background LRU GC. :thumbsup:
